$comment: DEALER BRAND FILE. The only file you edit to rebrand the whole campaign. Run `npm run build` after editing.
$status: Colors and type lockup derived from a screenshot of bobjohnsonautogroup.com supplied by the client; hex values were read off the image rather than the stylesheet, so they are close, confirm against the real brand sheet. Upgraded to the multi-dealer schema on 30 Sep 2026: the sending, supabase and metricbridge blocks below used to be hardcoded in the single-dealer engine and are now read from here, the same as every other dealership. Provenance for each block is in its own $comment.

color.$note: Black, gold and white. Gold is eyedropped from the specials bar and the primary buttons.
color.accentDarkNote: Added with the multi-dealer engine, which needs a dark variant of accent for 9px legal and eyebrow type: the gold does not carry enough contrast on white at that size. Darkened from the same hue rather than sampled. Never used as a button ground.
color.onAccentNote: Black, because the gold is a light accent. Do not copy the white used on Ferrario's red.

logo.$note: REPLACE with a hosted absolute https URL. Until then the header renders a type lockup that matches the wordmark: black italic extrabold name over a gold rule, with AUTO GROUP letterspaced beneath. That fallback is also what any recipient with images disabled will see, so it is worth keeping good.

contact.addressNote: CONFIRMED by client: Rochester is the first rooftop in this program. If a later dealership in the group is added, give it its own dealer file rather than changing this one.

campaign.idNote: Distinct from Ferrario on purpose. vsc_enrollment and vsc_email_template are keyed on (dealer_id, campaign_id, ...), so a shared id would put two dealerships in one campaign namespace.
campaign.unsubscribeNote: The deployed Supabase Edge Function. Keyed per recipient and scoped by dealer_id in the URL, so dealerships share it without touching each other's opt outs. Set both UNSUBSCRIBE_URL_BASE and PREFERENCES_URL_BASE to this.

brandLead.$comment: dealer means the dealership colour leads the layout and DriveOne is reduced to the provider mark in the header. Correct for a send made on their behalf, and the same mode Ferrario uses.
brandLead.$change: BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, flagged rather than buried. The single-dealer engine had no brandLead and rendered every structural accent in DriveOne cyan regardless of the dealership. Under the multi-dealer engine an absent brandLead would have kept that cyan, so this is set explicitly to dealer: hero rules, buttons and icon strokes now resolve to Bob Johnson gold. Re-review a filled preview before his next send, because his emails will not look the way they did when they were last built.

metricbridge.$comment: From the MetricBridge dealer record as recorded in docs/METRICBRIDGE.md, read live on 28 Sep 2026. Not re-queried during the multi-dealer merge, so re-confirm if MetricBridge has since split rooftops.
metricbridge.down_payment_note: 0.05 on the partner record, corroborating the 5% in emails 1 and 5.
metricbridge.rooftopNote: The MetricBridge record is group level, Bob Johnson Auto on bobjohnsonauto.com, while this campaign targets the Watertown CDJR rooftop. If MetricBridge splits rooftops, point this at the Watertown record. Note this dealer file's own display name is the Rochester store, which is the same unresolved rooftop-versus-group question the artwork settled for Ferrario. Worth closing before his next send.

supabase.$comment: From docs/SUPABASE.md, measured 28 Sep 2026. partners.id here equals dealers.source_id in MetricBridge, which is the join between the two systems.
supabase.partner_type_note: Ferrario uses 'service-drive-ferrario'. Do not copy either value across.
supabase.initial_cohort_note: 150 of the 364 who would enrol at a 90 day window. Total sends are cohort x 10 however slowly people are fed in, so cohort is the only lever that lowers volume.
supabase.intake_window_note: A 30 day window enrols 107 and strands 350. At 90 days it is 364.
supabase.max_mileage_note: Effectively off. The rating API is keyed on VIN and decides what it can rate; a local ceiling only second guesses it.
supabase.data_quality_note: UNRESOLVED and inconsistent between two documents in this repo, left flagged rather than silently picked. docs/SUPABASE.md records has_existing_warranty as null for all 474 of his rows, measured 28 Sep. brand/dealers/ferrario-ford.json records the column as fully populated at BOTH stores with zero nulls, 37 true and 410 false for Bob Johnson, checked 30 Sep. Both cannot be true. The likely reading is that the column was backfilled between those dates, which would make the doc stale rather than wrong, but that has not been verified against the live database. Intake filters `= false`, which excludes nulls as well as trues, so if the column really is null his intake returns nobody. Re-query before enrolling him again.

sending.$comment: These were hardcoded in the single-dealer engine and are reproduced here from the Throughput and timing table in the campaign skill, which documents them as Bob Johnson's own settings. Ferrario's file carries the same numbers, copied from his deliberately.
sending.dailyCapNote: Hard ceiling per calendar day in dealer local time, enforced inside the atomic claim so two scheduler runs cannot jointly exceed it.
sending.daysNote: Tuesday through Friday. Monday is excluded because Monday inboxes are cleared in bulk. Friday is INCLUDED for an arithmetic reason rather than a preference: two days drawn from Tue/Wed/Thu alone can only ever be 1, 2, 5, 6 or 7 days apart, so the 3 and 4 day gaps the deck opens with are impossible to express and every gap silently collapses to 7. Do not narrow this without re-running n8n/verify.mjs.
sending.hoursNote: Local. Mid morning and early afternoon, skipping the lunch hour.
sending.maxPerRunNote: Ceiling on any single hourly run, so a backlog cannot arrive as one spike.
sending.fromNote:
DECIDED 1 Oct 2026: send on a per-dealer subdomain of a DriveOne root, not on the dealership's own domain and not on a Kovara domain.

Why a DriveOne root. Ferrario's sending mailbox turned out to live on Captured's server, which nobody can reach. The Kovara domains were offered as warm alternatives and rejected: they are the dealer-acquisition cold prospecting stack, and copy that says 'the service department you drove to' cannot ship from getkovara.com.

Why a SUBDOMAIN and not the root. driveoneprogram.com is a live Google Workspace domain carrying real people's mailboxes. Putting 3,500 consumer sends on the root would do to DriveOne's own corporate mail exactly what sending from ferrario.com risked doing to the dealership's. The subdomain also leaves the root SPF untouched, which matters because a domain gets exactly one.

Why PER DEALER. Reputation then fails per rooftop, the same way dist, workflows and campaign ids already separate per rooftop. A complaint spike at one dealership does not reach another's customers. It also puts the dealership's name in the visible From domain, which is the next best thing to sending from their own.

The root is one field to change if the client prefers driveonepartners.com or driveonedealers.com; all three are on Vercel DNS with the same Google MX, the same `~all` SPF and the same `p=none` DMARC, so the setup is identical. Do NOT use driveonedirect.com, which is the DTC money site, or driveonenow.com, which has no MX at all.

n8n's SEND_FROM must read `fromName <fromAddress>` and is checked at launch.
